title: Sprint 4 — Permissions, Error Handling & Automated Testing
description: Enforce custom DRF object-level permission classes, author automated API test suites using APITestCase, standardize error handling, and author complete REST API documentation.

tickets.title: TODO-010: Enforce Authentication and Object-Level Permissions
tickets.description:
### Overview
Conduct a comprehensive security audit of all API endpoints and implement a reusable custom DRF permission class named `IsOwner`. In `tasks/permissions.py`, create `IsOwner(permissions.BasePermission)` and implement `has_object_permission(self, request, view, obj)` to ensure that `obj.owner == request.user`. Apply `[IsAuthenticated, IsOwner]` across all task views. Verify that public authentication endpoints (`/api/auth/register/`, `/api/auth/login/`) remain accessible with `[AllowAny]`, while all task endpoints strictly reject unauthorized requests with HTTP 401 Unauthorized or HTTP 403 Forbidden / 404 Not Found.

### Dependencies
- `TODO-007`: Implement Update Task API.
- `TODO-008`: Implement Delete Task API.
- `TODO-009`: Implement Task Completion Status API.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Custom permission class `IsOwner` is created in `tasks/permissions.py` inheriting from `rest_framework.permissions.BasePermission`.
- [ ] `has_object_permission` returns `True` only when `obj.owner == request.user`.
- [ ] All task endpoints (`/api/tasks/`, `/api/tasks/<pk>/`, `/api/tasks/<pk>/status/`) require authentication (`IsAuthenticated`).
- [ ] Detail endpoints enforce `IsOwner` so users cannot read, update, delete, or toggle tasks belonging to another user.
- [ ] Cross-user access attempts return HTTP 403 Forbidden or HTTP 404 Not Found.
- [ ] Public authentication endpoints (`/api/auth/register/`, `/api/auth/login/`) explicitly allow unauthenticated access (`[AllowAny]`).
- [ ] Missing, malformed, or invalid tokens consistently return HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

### Expected Deliverables
- `tasks/permissions.py` containing `IsOwner` class.
- Updated `tasks/views.py` with consistent permission classes.

### Evaluation Criteria
- Security test: User A with a valid token attempting to access User B's task receives 403 or 404.
- Unauthenticated request to `/api/tasks/` receives 401.
- Public endpoints remain accessible without tokens.
learning_objectives: Create custom object-level permission classes in Django REST Framework.
Implement has_object_permission to inspect model instances against request.user.
Differentiate between view-level permissions (IsAuthenticated) and object-level permissions (IsOwner).
Maintain consistent authentication challenges across RESTful APIs.

tasks.title: Task 1 — Implement Custom IsOwner Permission Class
tasks.description: Create `tasks/permissions.py` and implement `class IsOwner(permissions.BasePermission)`. Implement `has_object_permission(self, request, view, obj)` returning `obj.owner == request.user`.

tasks.title: Task 2 — Audit and Apply Permissions to All Endpoints
tasks.description: Audit all API views in `tasks/views.py`. Set `permission_classes = [permissions.AllowAny]` on Register and Login. Set `permission_classes = [permissions.IsAuthenticated, IsOwner]` on all task views.

common_mistakes: Implementing has_permission instead of has_object_permission, which doesn't receive the model instance.
Locking down the registration or login endpoints by applying IsAuthenticated globally without overriding it with AllowAny.
Relying solely on frontend validation rather than server-side permission checks.
hints:
In `tasks/permissions.py`:
```python
from rest_framework import permissions
class IsOwner(permissions.BasePermission):
    def has_object_permission(self, request, view, obj):
        return obj.owner == request.user
```
Remember that `has_object_permission` is only invoked when `self.get_object()` is called in detail views.

tickets.title: TODO-011: Implement Automated API Tests
tickets.description:
### Overview
Author a comprehensive automated test suite for the entire REST API using Django REST Framework's testing utilities (`rest_framework.test.APITestCase` and `APIClient`). In `tasks/tests.py`, write unit and integration test cases covering: (1) User registration with valid and invalid payloads; (2) User login, token generation, and logout token invalidation; (3) Task CRUD operations (create, list, retrieve, update, delete, status toggle); (4) Input validation errors (missing title, non-boolean status); (5) Unauthenticated access rejections; and (6) Cross-user isolation and ownership permission enforcement. All tests must execute cleanly via `python manage.py test`.

### Dependencies
- `TODO-010`: Enforce Authentication and Object-Level Permissions.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tasks/tests.py` uses `APITestCase` and DRF's `APIClient`.
- [ ] Authentication tests verify successful registration (201), duplicate registration rejection (400), valid login with token receipt (200), invalid login (400/401), and logout (200).
- [ ] Task CRUD tests verify creation with token (201), listing only user's tasks (200), single task retrieval (200), full update (200), partial update (200), deletion (204), and status update (200).
- [ ] Validation tests verify missing required fields return HTTP 400 Bad Request.
- [ ] Security tests verify unauthenticated requests to `/api/tasks/` return HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
- [ ] Cross-user security tests verify that User A cannot view, update, delete, or toggle User B's task (returns 404 or 403).
- [ ] All tests run and pass with 0 failures or errors via `python manage.py test`.

### Expected Deliverables
- `tasks/tests.py` containing test classes (`AuthAPITests`, `TaskCRUDAPITests`, `TaskSecurityAPITests`).

### Evaluation Criteria
- Running `python manage.py test` exits with code 0.
- Minimum of 10 automated test methods covering all API endpoints and status codes.
- Complete isolation between tests with independent fixtures and clean teardowns.
learning_objectives: Write robust API tests using rest_framework.test.APITestCase.
Assert JSON response payloads, status codes, and database states.
Test boundary conditions, invalid inputs, and security permissions.

tasks.title: Task 1 — Authentication API Tests
tasks.description: In `tasks/tests.py`, implement `AuthAPITests` testing registration success (201), duplicate username (400), valid login (200 with token), invalid login (400/401), and logout (200). Assert token deletion.

tasks.title: Task 2 — Task CRUD and Security API Tests
tasks.description: Implement `TaskAPITests` testing task creation, list filtering by user, detail retrieval, PUT/PATCH updates, DELETE (204), PATCH status, unauthenticated 401 checks, and cross-user 404/403 access attempts.

common_mistakes: Using standard Django TestCase/Client instead of DRF's APITestCase/APIClient, losing native JSON request helpers.
Not setting client.credentials(HTTP_AUTHORIZATION='Token ' + token.key) before issuing authenticated requests.
Testing only happy paths while neglecting 400, 401, 403, and 404 status assertions.
hints: Use `self.client.credentials(HTTP_AUTHORIZATION='Token ' + self.token.key)` to authenticate the client.

solution.tests_py:
from rest_framework.test import APITestCase
from rest_framework import status
from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from rest_framework.authtoken.models import Token
from tasks.models import Task

class TaskSecurityAPITests(APITestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.user1 = User.objects.create_user('user1', 'u1@test.com', 'pass123')
        self.user2 = User.objects.create_user('user2', 'u2@test.com', 'pass123')
        self.token1 = Token.objects.create(user=self.user1)
        self.token2 = Token.objects.create(user=self.user2)
        self.task1 = Task.objects.create(owner=self.user1, title='User1 Task')

    def test_unauthenticated_request_rejected(self):
        response = self.client.get('/api/tasks/')
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED)

    def test_user_cannot_access_other_task(self):
        self.client.credentials(HTTP_AUTHORIZATION='Token ' + self.token2.key)
        response = self.client.get(f'/api/tasks/{self.task1.id}/')
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND)

tickets.title: TODO-012: Standardize API Responses and Documentation
tickets.description:
### Overview
Finalize the REST API project by ensuring consistent error and success response structures and authoring comprehensive API documentation. Create a detailed `README.md` and/or `docs/api_documentation.md` describing all endpoints, HTTP methods, authentication headers, request body schemas with sample JSON payloads, successful response examples with status codes, and standard error formats (400, 401, 403, 404). Include setup instructions detailing virtual environment configuration, dependency installation, migration execution, server launch, and automated test running. Absolutely no frontend or HTML templates should be introduced.

### Dependencies
- `TODO-011`: Implement Automated API Tests.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `README.md` is authored with complete technical documentation for the REST API.
- [ ] All 7 API endpoints are fully documented: `GET /api/health/`, `POST /api/auth/register/`, `POST /api/auth/login/`, `POST /api/auth/logout/`, `GET & POST /api/tasks/`, `GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE /api/tasks/<int:pk>/`, and `PATCH /api/tasks/<int:pk>/status/`.
- [ ] Each endpoint includes HTTP method, URL path, required headers (e.g. `Authorization: Token <key>`), request JSON schema/example, and response JSON example with HTTP status codes.
- [ ] Standard error formats (400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found) are clearly specified with sample payloads.
- [ ] Setup documentation includes: Python virtual environment creation, `pip install -r requirements.txt`, database migrations (`python manage.py migrate`), running the server (`python manage.py runserver`), and running automated tests (`python manage.py test`).
- [ ] Contains sample `curl` commands or Postman instructions for testing endpoints.
- [ ] No frontend, HTML templates, CSS, or JavaScript files are added.

### Expected Deliverables
- `README.md` (or `docs/api_documentation.md`) containing complete API reference and developer setup instructions.
- `requirements.txt` listing `django`, `djangorestframework`, etc.

### Evaluation Criteria
- Documentation accuracy: All endpoints, methods, parameters, and responses in docs match actual API implementation.
- Cleanliness check: Zero frontend assets, templates, or HTML views exist in the repository.
- Reproducibility: A new developer can set up and run tests solely using the documentation.
learning_objectives: Document RESTful APIs with endpoint specifications and curl/Postman examples.
Establish standardized error response formats across an API.
Produce professional developer setup guides for backend microservices.
Maintain clean architectural boundaries without frontend coupling.

solution.readme_md:
# Django ToDo REST API

A backend-only REST API built with Django, Django REST Framework, and SQLite.

## Quick Start
```bash
python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
python manage.py migrate
python manage.py runserver
```

## Running Tests
```bash
python manage.py test
```

## API Endpoints
- `POST /api/auth/register/` - Register user
- `POST /api/auth/login/` - Login & obtain token
- `POST /api/auth/logout/` - Invalidate token
- `GET /api/tasks/` - List user tasks
- `POST /api/tasks/` - Create task
- `GET /api/tasks/<id>/` - Retrieve task
- `PUT/PATCH /api/tasks/<id>/` - Update task
- `DELETE /api/tasks/<id>/` - Delete task
- `PATCH /api/tasks/<id>/status/` - Update completion status
